A1.justification: Both PDFs describe X-SG2S, and all supplied text, equations, tables and figures are readable. Neither supplied PDF includes an appendix, although v3 Section 3.4 explicitly refers to an appendix containing further DCAE details. Those promised details cannot be compared.

before.justification: V2 reports original watermark-recovery, rendering-fidelity, pruning-robustness and ablation results in Tables 1–5 and Figures 7–9.

after.justification: V3 reports original watermarking experiments, including baseline comparisons, perturbation tests, ablations and capacity analyses in Tables 1–7 and Figure 8.

M1.justification: V2's training steps and Figure 5 pass watermarked points directly to recovery. V3 Section 3.3 and Figure 2 explicitly introduce training-time cropout, noise, rotation and translation before recovery. The patching strategy, selection gates, injection/extraction heads and loss components otherwise remain substantially unchanged.

E1.justification: ACID scenes, binary messages, Logo-2K images and Objaverse/Gamba object payloads remain. V3 additionally reports evaluation on Mip-NeRF360 in Table 1 and Blender/LLFF in Table 2. Watermark recovery is also tested under SH noise, translation and rotation, extending v2's point-removal coverage.

E2.justification: V2 evaluates internal variants but provides no external-method comparison. V3 Table 2 adds five baseline configurations: fine-tuned 3DGS, GaussianMarker with 2D and 3D decoders, GuardSplat and 3D-GSW, evaluated against X-SG2S on 48-bit watermark recovery.

E3.justification: Default loss weights change from gamma=0.2 and theta=0.8 to gamma=1 and theta=2. V3 adds a 48-bit baseline-comparison protocol, capacity sweeps and specified geometric/SH perturbations. Original dataset splits, rendering resolutions and default payload sizes remain. The noise setting is inconsistent within v3: Section 4.4 states sigma=0.1, while Tables 1–2 state 0.05.

E4.justification: V3 adds payload-versus-rendering-distortion sweeps and noise, translation and rotation robustness analyses. It removes the Addition and Concatenation gate-fusion ablations, retaining the multiplicative method, Normal and Random variants. V2's 5–25% pruning sweep survives as Cropout testing; higher-order-SH, modality and optional-loss analyses also remain.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. V3 continues reporting point estimates despite expanding the experiments.

E6.justification: Corresponding scene/image/object PSNR entries change from 27.666/30.537/21.140 in v2 Table 1 to 27.804/22.791/23.017 in v3 Table 6 under revised settings. At 25% point removal, bit recovery changes from 100% to 97.7%. New baseline, attack and capacity results are reported; v3 Table 2 shows X-SG2S below GaussianMarker's 3D decoder under SH noise, 94.12% versus 99.90%. These are revised or additional results, not established same-setting gains.

T1.justification: The projected-covariance expression changes from J W Sigma_i J^T W^T in v2 Section 3.1 to J_i Sigma_i J_i^T in v3 Equation 2, with J_i defined as the local projection Jacobian. This is a localized mathematical revision; the attention and loss formulations are otherwise restated, without new theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The central claim of simultaneous 1D-to-3D watermarking remains. V3 adds explicit embedding-within-seconds and higher-capacity-than-existing-methods claims. It also strengthens preservation of the parameter form to 'zero modifications to parameters,' despite retaining SH-parameter replacement in the method.

C2.justification: V3 adds a substantive capacity–distortion interpretation: larger binary payloads degrade rendering quality, although the reported interference remains limited. Its gate-ablation discussion shifts from selecting among fusion strategies to emphasizing the benefit of Gaussian–watermark interaction. Existing redundancy and optional-loss explanations largely remain.

D1.justification: The reported GPU changes from RTX4090 to RTX A6000ada, and two loss weights are revised. V3 Table 2 newly reports embedding-time estimates. V2's explicit SH-order indices and DCAE latent dimensions are no longer specified, and the appendix promised for additional DCAE details is absent. Neither version supplies code-access instructions.

R1.justification: V3 adds a Watermarking in Deep Learning subsection discussing HiDDeN, HiNet, VideoSeal and Videomark, and positions X-SG2S against GuardSplat and 3D-GSW. The generation discussion replaces Instant3D with DiffGS. These changes substantially broaden the prior-work discussion beyond v2's primarily 3D-focused positioning.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, contribution list, method exposition and conclusion undergo extensive rewriting. Method subsections are consolidated and reordered, dataset/metric descriptions are grouped, and ablations move behind fidelity, robustness and baseline comparisons. The author and affiliation block is also revised.

P2.justification: The document switches from two-column to single-column layout. Application and training diagrams are redrawn; the separate patching schematic and five-variant interaction diagram disappear. A baseline table and capacity plots are added, qualitative montages are reduced or rearranged, and several tables are transposed or gain reference columns.

improvement.justification: V3 gives v2's largely unbenchmarked performance claims useful support through external comparisons, broader perturbation tests and the capacity–distortion analysis, while improving organization. The gain is limited by sparse documentation of the added benchmarks, conflicting noise settings, the missing referenced appendix and stronger parameter-preservation claims that conflict with SH replacement. The evidence base improves, but these reporting problems prevent a clear substantial overall improvement.
